EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A human triggered avalanche occurred on December 9th in the area of Long Pass in Kittitas county. The avalanche was preceded by a multi day heavy snow event that saw 1 to 2 feet of snow fall in the region.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper-level trough moving through the region combined with cooling temperatures aloft and daytime heating to facilitate shower and thunderstorm activity. A shower was strong enough to produce a cold-air funnel along the coast in addition to a short lived thunderstorm producing strong outflow winds in southwest Washington.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An unusually intense storm was able to generate a strong downdraft despite limited environmental support, which resulted in a narrow damage swath in Meadow Glade, WA in Clark County. NWS Portland conducted a damage survey in the affected area on Sunday, June 7. NWS storm surveyors found a small area at the  west end of the storm track which experienced heavier damage,  including a metal roof peeled back from an outbuilding and  multiple hardwood trees with trunks snapped multiple feet above  ground level. These damage indicators suggest a maximum wind speed  of just over 90 mph. As the storm moved east, associated wind  speeds weakened, producing minor damage including small downed or  broken tree limbs, lifted roof shingles, and damaged fences,  corresponding to wind speeds of 50-65 mph.
